claim_verdicts.evidence: Ablation on the same lab setup: with kindnet (stage-3 cni.txt) donhang-worker has "10.244.0.0/24 via 172.22.0.2 dev eth0" and "10.244.1.0/24 via 172.22.0.4 dev eth0", one per other node, to that node's address; with disableDefaultCNI (stage-4 cni-off.txt) the worker's only via line is "default via 172.22.0.1 dev eth0". So the Pod-range routes come with kindnet; they are plain kernel routes on dev eth0, no tunnel device, so the node forwards by them. Observed on donhang-worker; other nodes run the same DaemonSet Pod (claim 6).
claim_verdicts.source: examples/don-hang outputs/stage-3/scripts/k8s/cni.txt (stage-3); outputs/stage-4/scripts/k8s/cni-off.txt, scripts/k8s/cni-off.sh (stage-4, new script; cni.sh unchanged stage-3..stage-4)

issues.quote: False, because a router on the way looks at the Pod address and has no route for it, so the packet needs another way across, such as being carried inside a packet between node addresses.
issues.text: Round 2, new in the reworded option. Option c is now about twice as long as a, b and d, and is the only one that explains a mechanism step by step. I could pick it by length alone without following the reasoning.
issues.fix: Shorten option c to about the length of the others, e.g. 'False: routers on the way have no route for the Pod address the packet still carries.', or lengthen b with a similar because-clause.

issues.quote: Without a plugin, the runtime cannot connect any Pod that uses the Pod network
issues.text: Round 2, new in the narrowed sentence. 'a Pod that uses the Pod network' implies some Pods do not, but I only learn that a Pod can use its node's network one section later. Here I stopped and wondered which Pods are excluded.
issues.fix: Add a few words after 'Pod network': '(a Pod can instead use its node's network, as kindnet's own Pods do below)'.
